title: Equivariant marked plurinodal alteration over a field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $X$ a normal proper geometrically integral finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $Z\subseteq X$ an invariant nowhere dense closed subset. Normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. Let a finite group $H$ act faithfully on $X$ by scheme automorphisms and on $k$ by field automorphisms, compatibly with the structure map. There are a finite extension $F/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] [def-pc-field-tower], a finite group $J$ with a surjection $ho:J	o H$, an action on $F$ extending the $H$-action on $k$, a tower of integral schemes $T_d\xrightarrow{f_d}\cdots\xrightarrow{f_1}T_0=\operatorname{Spec}F$, with $d=\dim X$, and a $J$-equivariant projective surjective generically finite morphism $a:T_d	o X$ [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Each $f_i$ is projective, flat and finitely presented, has nonempty geometrically connected reduced one-dimensional fibres with only ordinary double points, and has smooth geometrically integral generic fibre. An ordinary double point has completed geometric local ring $\Omega[[x,y]]/(xy)$. Each $f_i$ has finitely many disjoint sections $s_{i
u}$ in its relative smooth locus. Set $Z_0=\varnothing$ and $Z_i=f_i^{-1}Z_{i-1}\cup igcup_
u s_{i
u}(T_{i-1})$ as closed sets. The map $f_i$ is smooth away from $Z_{i-1}$, and $a^{-1}Z\subseteq Z_d$. The tower is $J$-equivariant, its unions of sections are stable, and it is quasi-split: every node of every fibre and its two inverse images in the normalization are rational over the residue field of the base point. The group may permute sections and fibre graphs; no triviality of stabilizer actions on marked legs is asserted. Writing $N=\kerho$, the extension $F^N/k$ is purely inseparable. There is a dense open $U\subseteq X$ with $a^{-1}U	o U$ finite surjective and with every geometric fibre a single $N$-orbit. Generically finite means finite over a dense open. The tower of length zero is $T_0=\operatorname{Spec}F$. Flatness, finite presentation and smoothness use [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; fibres, sections and finite morphisms use [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-weil-closed-immersion] and [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Dimension is [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

proof.text: Induct strongly on $d$, allowing nonfaithful input actions and requiring an H-projective map and $k(T_d)^{\ker(J\to H)}/k(X)$ purely inseparable. For $d=0$, properness gives $X=\operatorname{Spec}L$ finite over $k$; geometric integrality forces $L=k$ (a separable part splits and a nontrivial inseparable part gives nilpotents over an algebraic closure). Take $F=k,J=H,a=\mathrm{id}$; $Z=\varnothing$, as a nowhere dense closed subset of a point is empty. For $d=1$, apply the one-curve reduction with $C=X,Y=\operatorname{Spec}k,E=Z$: its $B=\operatorname{Spec}e,D=\varnothing$ give $F=e,J=G,T_1=V,a=c$, H-projective; $V\to B$ is smooth as $D=\varnothing$, $c^{-1}Z$ lies in the sections, and both fixed-field assertions hold.

source.place: X Lemma 2.2 proof, pp.149--150; de Jong 1997 Theorem 5.9 proof p.617, dimension induction and final cartesian construction; repair assembly step 1

proof.text: For $d\geq2$ take the equivariant pencil $X'\to Y$ and $\pi:X'\to X$. Apply one-curve reduction to $E=\pi^{-1}Z$, $H$-stable, and nowhere dense since $\pi$ is an isomorphism over a dense open and preserves the generic point. Write its output as $v:V\to B,c:V\to X',b:B\to Y,e,G\xrightarrow\alpha H,D$. Finite type over a field makes the schemes Noetherian; $b$ is proper with finite function-field extension, so the dimension lemma gives $\dim B=\dim Y=d-1$ (topological dimension, the same over $e$). Induction on $(B,D,G)$ gives $h:P\to B$, a tower over $F/e$ and $J\xrightarrow\beta G$. Set $A=\ker\alpha,Q=\ker\beta,N=\ker(\alpha\beta)$. Retain $e^A/k,k(V)^A/k(X'),F^Q/e,k(P)^Q/k(B)$ purely inseparable.

source.place: X Lemma 2.2 proof, pp.149--150; de Jong 1997 Theorem 5.9 proof p.617, dimension induction and final cartesian construction; repair assembly step 2

proof.text: Apply the flat-curve pullback lemma with $K=k(B),L=k(V),M=k(P)$: $W=V\times_B P$ is integral and $k(W)=L\otimes_K M$ is finite over $L$. Apply the cartesian tower-extension lemma to $v,h,c,\pi$ and the inductive boundaries. It appends $W\to P$, gives the diagonal action and pulled-back markings, all quasi-split nodal and smoothness clauses, $a^{-1}Z\subseteq Z_d$, and H-projectivity, surjectivity and finite function-field extension for $a=\pi c\operatorname{pr}_V$.

source.place: X Lemma 2.2 proof, pp.149--150; de Jong 1997 Theorem 5.9 proof p.617, dimension induction and final cartesian construction; repair assembly step 3

proof.text: The surjection $N\to A$ has kernel $Q$, which acts trivially on $L$. Apply the tensor-kernel invariant lemma with $R=k(X')=k(X)$ ($\pi$ birational) and $M^Q/K$ from induction. It gives $k(W)^N/k(X)$ purely inseparable. Its constant-field clause applied to $k\subseteq e\subseteq F$ gives $F^N/k$ purely inseparable. This closes the strengthened induction. In every dimension apply the generic invariant-field orbit-open lemma to the constructed H-projective surjection $a$ and its kernel $N$. It supplies the dense open with finite surjective restriction and nonempty single $N$-orbit geometric fibres. An H-projective $a$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense with $\mathcal E=\mathcal O_X^{n+1}$, as $\mathbf P_X(\mathcal O_X^{n+1})=\mathbf P^n_X$. All clauses of the unchanged statement follow.
